newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Banks propose Philippine Europeso issue.
newsitem.headline: Banks propose Philippine Europeso issue.

text.p: Two more investment banks have approached the Philippines to issue a Europeso debt instrument, finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Wednesday.
"There are a number of institutions that have approached us," de Ocampo told Reuters Financial Television.
He said the International Finance Corp (IFC) of the World Bank and Bank of Tokyo have presented their respective proposals to issue a peso-denominated debt paper in the international debt market.
The idea was first broached by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, a subsidiary of Deutsche Bank. ING Barings Philippines and Merrill Lynch followed up with their own proposals.
He said the finance department is still studying the different options presented by the investment houses.
One option is to have IFC, a triple A institution, float the instrument on behalf of the government, or to issue a limited amount in order to create a benchmark for such issues.
If at all the government goes through with the issue, it will be in the first half of next year, de Ocampo said.
